new_findings.mechanism: In the opt-in UOS_MCP_WIRE_MODE=canonical stdio mode, canonical_loop handles Error(error) from ingest_canonical by printing error.code and returning Nil, so one oversized frame, textual or escaped NUL, duplicate member, depth-33 frame, or frame-deadline violation terminates the stdio gateway process (the -eval then reaches halt(0)) with no JSON-RPC error emitted to the client. This contradicts the J1 'never terminates before EOF' property that standard_loop (4168-4212) does satisfy, and matches the rmcp #557 DoS class the journals claim to have closed. Reachability: no pinned client configuration (.mcp.json, .pi/mcp.json, .gemini/settings.json, .codex/config.toml, user-level configs) sets UOS_MCP_WIRE_MODE; the launcher merely documents the variable; no test, receipt or Lean model covers canonical mode. Not a falsification of any sealed claim, which are all scoped to standard_loop.
new_findings.recommendation: Either recurse canonical_loop after emitting a standard_response refusal (as the ReadError arm already does) or remove the canonical mode from the launcher help; add a fault-survival test for the mode if retained.

new_findings.mechanism: The R04-02 wedge (orphan native guardian) is closed, but the third interim recommendation was not adopted: ensure_mcp_tables still raises error(mcp_tables_failed|mcp_tables_timeout|mcp_guardian_recovery_timeout) rather than returning {error,Reason}. with_inflight_slot and with_native_workspace_slot catch it and refuse, but gateway_handle_new, durable_initial and cached_supervised_gateway (owner child-start/boot path) let the raise propagate into the OneForOne restart budget (20/60 s). The durable-ledger guardian name is still taken with unguarded true=register(...) at 1188 (fresh guardian) and 1240 (heir takeover); both are protected only by the ETS-presence precondition and the global:trans boot lock, and await_mcp_guardian allows 200 ms for heir registration while mcp_heir_takeover may wait up to 1000 ms for a missing ETS-TRANSFER.
new_findings.recommendation: Return typed errors from ensure_mcp_tables and translate them to GATEWAY_UNAVAILABLE/Retryable at the three boot-path callers; wrap the two ledger-guardian register calls in the same badarg-adopt pattern as ensure_native_guardian.

new_findings.mechanism: The R04-11 headless fallback expands ${HOME} under set -u, so a systemd or cron context with HOME unset fails with a bash 'unbound variable' message instead of the launcher's own diagnostic (fail-closed but opaque, the exact symptom R04-11 set out to remove); the verifier result is parsed with an unpinned host `jq` from PATH (absent jq -> 'full capsule verification failed'), while every other toolchain path in the script is pinned. The controlled-predicate test (headless-cache-final-observation.json) left HOME set and jq present, so neither path was exercised.
new_findings.recommendation: Guard with ${HOME:-} plus an explicit error, and either pin jq from the Nix profile or parse the verifier JSON with the already-pinned OCaml binary.
